Abbreviation Glossary From a Label Dictionary

Source: R/report_text_helpers.R
tbl_abbreviations_glossary.Rd

Turns the label dictionary used by [pretty_name()] into an abbreviation reference table for a report appendix: abbreviation (short label), definition (full label), unit and domain.

Usage

tbl_abbreviations_glossary(
  dict,
  domains = NULL,
  only_abbreviations = TRUE,
  include_term = FALSE
)

Arguments

dict

A data frame with a term column (`term`, `variable`, `name`, ...), a short-label column (`short`, `abbreviation`, `label`) and a full-label column (`full`, `definition`, `description`), and optionally `unit` and `domain` columns. Column names are matched without regard to case.

domains

Optional character vector of domains to keep, in the order given. Needs a `domain` column.

only_abbreviations

If `TRUE` (default), entries whose short and full labels are the same, or that lack one of them, are left out: they are not abbreviations.

include_term

If `TRUE`, the raw column name is kept as the first column. Default `FALSE`.

Value

A tibble with `Abbreviation`, `Definition`, and `Unit` / `Domain` when the dictionary has them, one row per distinct abbreviation and definition, sorted by domain (in `domains` order, or alphabetically) and then by abbreviation without regard to case.

See also

[pretty_name()], [tbl_label_map()]

Examples

dict <- data.frame(
  term = c("liv_rl", "thb_osm3", "age"),
  short = c("LIV (%RL)", "tHb", "Age"),
  full = c("Lung injury volume", "Total hemoglobin", "Age"),
  unit = c("% right lung", "g/dL", "years"),
  domain = c("Imaging", "Blood", "Demographics")
)
tbl_abbreviations_glossary(dict)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   Abbreviation Definition         Unit         Domain 
#>   <chr>        <chr>              <chr>        <chr>  
#> 1 tHb          Total hemoglobin   g/dL         Blood  
#> 2 LIV (%RL)    Lung injury volume % right lung Imaging
pretty_name(c("liv_rl", "age", "not_in_dict"), dict = dict, form = "unit")
#> [1] "Lung injury volume (% right lung)" "Age (years)"                      
#> [3] "Not in Dict"
